    11	many minutes before. The earliest boundary a hook can reach after a narration line is the next tool
    12	call, which is the PreToolUse event. This scan sits there, so a correction reaches the human inside
    13	the same turn.

    16	hooks/turn_reader.py — the same reader the Stop-side scans use.

    19	  1. Naked internal codes, through code-anchor-scan.py's own matcher, imported rather than copied, so
    20	     the two arms can never drift into judging the same law differently.
    21	  2. Calques — the pack's internal English vocabulary loan-translated into the working language and
    22	     handed to the human as if it were his. The list is data, hooks/chat-calques.json, and each entry
    23	     carries the plain industry word the reply owed the reader, which the deny quotes.

    27	     this arm reads for it. The law's prose home is the writing register, rule 17.

   102	METHOD = re.compile(
   103	    r"`[^`\n]+`"
   104	    r"|\b[\w./-]+\.(?:py|sh|json|jsonl|md|log|txt|yml)\b"

   106	    r"|\b(?:measured|counted|produced|read|taken)\s+(?:by|with|from|off)\b"
   107	    # user-language: the same procedure words when chat runs in Russian
   108	    r"|измер\w+|посчита\w+|подсчита\w+|команд\w+|методом|скриптом|гейтом|по\s+записи",  # user-language
   109	    re.IGNORECASE,
   110	)

   112	BULLET_LINE = re.compile(r"^\s*(?:[-*+]\s|\d+[.)]\s)")

   114	_CODE_ANCHOR = []  # loaded once per process; the module compiles its patterns at import
   115	
   116	
   117	def _load_code_anchor():
   118	    """code-anchor-scan.py carries a dash in its name, so it is loaded by path rather than imported by
   119	    name. Its matcher is reused whole: one law, one set of patterns, two delivery points."""

   129	_CALQUES_CACHE = {}  # path -> compiled list; loaded once per process, not once per call
   130	
   131	
   132	def load_calques(path=CALQUES_PATH):
   133	    """The calque list as data: each entry's pattern compiled, with the plain word it asks for and its
   134	    cheap pre-filter keys. Compiled once per process and cached by path, since every call before this
   135	    change re-parsed the JSON and re-compiled all fifteen patterns even though the list never changes

   137	    if path in _CALQUES_CACHE:
   138	        return _CALQUES_CACHE[path]

   140	        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:

   148	        except (re.error, KeyError):

   158	
   159	def read_turn(transcript_path):

   161	
   162	
   163	def _quoted_spans_removed(text, anchor):
   164	    """Text ABOUT a word, rather than a word addressed to the reader, carries no offence.
   165	
   166	    A fenced block, an inline backtick span and a «quoted» or "quoted" span are the shapes the pack
   167	    already uses to name a word it is discussing, and code-anchor-scan.py's own patterns for them are
   168	    reused here. The correction this hook asks for quotes the calque and its replacement in exactly
   169	    that shape, so the correction itself reads clean.
   170	
   171	    The bracketed spans code-anchor-scan.py also strips are left standing: parentheses are the lawful
   172	    resting place of an internal CODE, and a calque inside them is still handed to the reader as his
   173	    own language.
   174	    """
   175	    text = anchor.FENCE.sub(" ", text)
   176	    text = anchor.INLINE_CODE.sub(" ", text)
   177	    return anchor.QUOTED.sub(" ", text)
   178	
   179	
   180	def _readable_window(text, start, end, reach):
   181	    """A context window cut back to whole words, so the correction quotes a readable fragment."""
   182	    left = max(0, start - reach)
   183	    right = min(len(text), end + reach)
   184	    if left > 0:
   185	        space = text.find(" ", left, start)
   186	        if space != -1:
   187	            left = space + 1
   188	    if right < len(text):
   189	        space = text.rfind(" ", end, right)
   190	        if space != -1:
   191	            right = space
   192	    return text[left:right].replace("\n", " ").strip()
   193	
   194	
   195	def blocks(text):
   196	    """The paragraphs a count is judged inside.
   197	
   198	    A measurement is stated with its parts in one block of prose, so the block is the window: a count in
   199	    one paragraph and a command three paragraphs later are two separate statements. A blank line closes
   200	    a block, and a list item opens one, since a bullet carries its own point.
   201	    """
   202	    out, current = [], []
   203	    for line in text.split("\n"):
   204	        if not line.strip() or BULLET_LINE.match(line):
   205	            if current:
   206	                out.append("\n".join(current))
   207	                current = []
   208	        if line.strip():
   209	            current.append(line)
   210	    if current:
   211	        out.append("\n".join(current))
   212	    return out
   213	
   214	
   215	def judge_measurements(text):
   216	    """Every count in the text whose block names no method, as findings of kind `measure`.
   217	
   218	    A fenced block is machine output rather than a sentence to the human, and a table row carries its
   219	    own describing cell, so both stand outside this reading. A backtick span stays IN, since a quoted
   220	    command is the commonest shape a method takes.
   221	    """
   222	    if not text:
   223	        return []
   224	    anchor = _load_code_anchor()
   225	    live = anchor.FENCE.sub(" ", text)
   226	    live = "\n".join(ln for ln in live.split("\n") if not ln.lstrip().startswith("|"))
   227	    findings = []
   228	    for block in blocks(live):
   229	        if METHOD.search(block):
   230	            continue
   231	        m = COUNT.search(block)
   232	        if not m:
   233	            continue
   234	        findings.append({
   235	            "kind": "measure",
   236	            "fragment": m.group().strip(),
   237	            "context": _readable_window(block, m.start(), m.end(), 60),
   238	            "say": "",
   239	        })

   241	
   242	
   243	def judge(text, calques=None):
   244	    """Every offence in the turn's text, as dicts carrying kind, fragment, context and replacement."""
   245	    if not text:
   246	        return []
   247	    findings = []
   248	
   249	    anchor = _load_code_anchor()
   250	    for fragment, context in anchor.find_matches(text):
   251	        findings.append({"kind": "code", "fragment": fragment, "context": context, "say": ""})
   252	
   253	    if calques is None:
   254	        calques = load_calques()
   255	    live = _quoted_spans_removed(text, anchor)
   256	    # The pre-filter: a plain substring test costs far less than a regex pass, so an entry with keys
   257	    # only pays for its expensive pattern when at least one of its keys is present. An entry with no
   258	    # keys (a missing or empty `keys` field) runs its pattern unconditionally, since a keyless entry has
   259	    # given the scan no cheap signal to filter on — silently skipping it would let a live law go dark.
   260	    low = live.lower()

   262	        if keys and not any(k in low for k in keys):
   263	            continue

   265	            findings.append({
   266	                "kind": "calque",
   267	                "word": word,
   268	                "fragment": m.group().strip(),
   269	                "context": _readable_window(live, m.start(), m.end(), 60),
   270	                "say": say,
   271	            })

   275	
   276	
   277	def fingerprint(finding):
   278	    """A fragment's identity: its own matched text, normalised. The surrounding context shifts as the
   279	    turn grows, so it can carry no part of the identity."""
   280	    core = " ".join(finding["fragment"].lower().split())
   281	    return hashlib.sha1((finding["kind"] + "|" + core).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]
   282	
   283	
   284	def _state_path(session_id, state_dir=STATE_DIR):

   286	    return os.path.join(state_dir, safe + ".json")
   287

   289	def read_reported(session_id, state_dir=STATE_DIR):

   291	        with open(_state_path(session_id, state_dir), encoding="utf-8") as fh:

   322	                         % (f["fragment"], f["say"], f["context"]))

   324	    if any(f["kind"] in ("code", "calque") for f in fresh):
   325	        tail += (
   326	            "\n\nA queue row number names nothing to a reader on its own, and a loan-translated internal "
   327	            "word names nothing to him at all. Say the sentence again in plain words in the very next "
   328	            "message, before anything else: name each wish in the product's own words with the code "
   329	            "trailing in parentheses, and use the plain industry word quoted above in place of each "
   330	            "calque."
   331	        )

   336	            "unit, and the method that produced it. State the count again in the very next message "
   337	            "with all four, naming the command or the procedure a reader runs to get the same number. "
   338	            "The rule's home is the writing register, rule 17."

   347	    )

   349	
   350	def is_main_session(payload):
   351	    """True only for a tool call made by the seat that talks to the human.
   352	
   353	    WHY THIS GUARD EXISTS (owner's word, 2026-08-16). This hook sits on PreToolUse with no matcher, so
   354	    it runs before EVERY tool call in the tree, a background worker's calls included. Its judgment is
   355	    always about the SEAT's narration — turn_reader skips sidechain records — so a worker's call was
   356	    denied and handed a correction naming a phrase that worker never wrote. Read from inside the
   357	    worker, that deny is an instruction from nowhere ordering it to rewrite someone else's sentence and
   358	    call again: the shape of a planted instruction, and it cost a night's trust to run down. The law
   359	    the hook carries is a law about what the HUMAN reads, so it belongs where the human reads.
   360	
   361	    HOW THE TWO SEATS ARE TOLD APART, by the transcript's own filename:
   362	        seat     ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<session_id>.jsonl
   363	        worker   ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<session_id>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl

   366	    on the worker side. An absent or unnamed path is treated as NOT the seat: a check that denies work
   367	    stands down when it cannot prove whose work it is.
   368	    """
   369	    path = payload.get("transcript_path") or ""
   370	    session_id = payload.get("session_id") or ""
   371	    if not path or not session_id:

   378	def main():

   380	        payload = json.load(sys.stdin)
   381	    except ValueError:
